title: Inborn Errors of Metabolism — Recognition & Workup
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Inborn Errors of Metabolism
Standard biochemical genetics teaching; regional newborn screening panels

changelog.change: Initial entry — when to suspect IEM (the sepsis-mimic trap), the disorders-by-category table, and the first-line blood/urine workup + management goals.

purpose: Recognise a metabolic crisis in a newborn who looks septic, send the right first-line labs BEFORE treatment changes the picture, and start the generic management (stop protein/offending substrate, high-calorie support, scavenge ammonia) while awaiting the specific diagnosis.
ageRange: Newborn to infant (classically a symptom-free interval then deterioration)

body.text: The trap: infants with an IEM are typically normal at birth and deteriorate over hours to weeks — closely mimicking late-onset sepsis. Send the metabolic panel with the septic work-up, not after it fails.

items: Unexplained neurologic deterioration, especially after a symptom-free interval.
Refractory hypoglycaemia, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, or hyperammonaemia.
Recurrent unexplained neonatal/infant deaths in the family; consanguinity.
An unusual odour, or hair/skin findings (sparse or brittle hair, eczema).

rows: Vomiting, liver failure, cataracts, E. coli sepsis after milk feeds → lactose/galactose-free formula
Vomiting, hypoglycaemia, liver dysfunction after fructose/sucrose → avoid fructose, sucrose, sorbitol
Normal at birth → intellectual disability if untreated; musty odour, fair hair/skin, eczema → lifelong low-phenylalanine diet; strict maternal control in pregnancy
Poor feeding, lethargy, maple-syrup odour, encephalopathy → BCAA-restricted diet; dialysis in acute crisis
Hyperammonaemia, vomiting, lethargy → coma, RESPIRATORY ALKALOSIS (early) → protein restriction, nitrogen scavengers (sodium benzoate/phenylacetate), dialysis if ammonia very high
Vomiting, lethargy, high-anion-gap acidosis with ketosis and hyperammonaemia → protein restriction, carnitine, B12 (in B12-responsive MMA)
Nuclear or mtDNA (maternal inheritance if mtDNA)
Multisystem: hypotonia, seizures, lactic acidosis, myopathy → supportive care, cofactor cocktails; avoid propofol infusions and valproate
Organomegaly, coarse facies, developmental regression → enzyme replacement, HSCT in selected disorders

items: Blood/plasma: CBC, glucose, electrolytes with anion gap, blood gas, AMMONIA (free-flowing, on ice, run immediately), lactate + pyruvate, plasma amino acids, acylcarnitine profile, total/free carnitine, LFTs.
Urine: pH, ketones, reducing substances, organic acids, acylglycines, orotic acid.
Save a 'critical sample' (extra plasma and urine, and a filter-paper card) during the acute crisis — diagnostic metabolites normalise quickly with treatment.

body.text: Generic management while awaiting results: stop protein and any offending substrate (lactose, fructose), give a high glucose infusion rate (GIR 8–10 mg/kg/min) to reverse catabolism, correct acidosis, start ammonia scavengers and arrange dialysis if the ammonia is markedly elevated, and supplement the cofactors most likely to help (carnitine, B12, biotin, thiamine, riboflavin) pending the specific diagnosis. Newborn bloodspot screening detects many treatable IEM before symptoms — know your region's panel, which varies.

buildNote: Recognition + generic acute management; the specific therapies are in the disorder table.
